issue: May the government withhold the third-level acceptance-of-responsibility motion under U.S.S.G. § 3E1.1(b) because the defendant in good faith objects to factual assertions in the presentence report or refuses to waive appeal rights?

sides.position: The government may not withhold the § 3E1.1(b) motion based on the defendant's refusal to waive appeal rights (Divens) or a good-faith objection to presentence report factual assertions (Lee).
cases: United States v. Divens, 650 F.3d 343 (4th Cir. 2011)
United States v. Lee, 653 F.3d 170 (2d Cir. 2011)

sides.position: The government has broad discretion to withhold the § 3E1.1(b) motion for any reason that does not violate the Constitution, including litigating contested relevant conduct at sentencing, which is a legitimate governmental interest.
cases: United States v. Nurek, 578 F.3d 624 (7th Cir. 2009)
United States v. Sainz-Preciado, 566 F.3d 713 (7th Cir. 2009)
United States v. Davis, 714 F.3d 474 (7th Cir. 2013)
United States v. Lafiamma Orona, 118 F.4th 858 (7th Cir. 2024)

this_court: Adheres to the Deberry line: Nurek and Sainz-Preciado remain binding, so objecting to relevant conduct is a legitimate basis for withholding the motion. Amendment 775 abrogated Deberry only on the appeal-waiver point and did not clearly displace Nurek and Sainz-Preciado.
quote: After our decisions in Deberry, Nurek, and Sainz-Preciado, a circuit split emerged on the scope of the government's discretion under § 3E1.1(b).
cite: United States v. Lafiamma Orona, 118 F.4th 858 (7th Cir. 2024)
